To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a novel, transcriptionally active group of pHMOs that are related to the SAR324 Deltasproteobacteria, a novel group that is related to the putative ethane-oxidizing Methylococcales and three novel groups of pHMO within gammaprotebacterial methanotrophic clades.

we discovered seven distinct phylogenetic clades of particulate hydrocarbon monooxgenases (pHMo) that were transcriptionally active in hydrothermal plume and background water metagenomes and that these clades included those related to putative ethane-oxidizing Methylococcae, a group of SAR324 Deltaprotoobacteria, three clades of deep sea gammaproteobacteria, one group related to Group Z, and one unknown group.

we have characterized the diversity of pHMO genes in the metagenomes and transcriptomes of hydrothermal vents and plumes, and have identified novel pHMO groups that are transcriptionally active in these environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes and organisms that are involved in hydrocarbon oxidation in a deep-sea ecosystem.
the diversity and function in hydrocarbon-rich hydrocarbon seep environments of genes involved in aerobic hydrocarbon degradation.
the diversity and function (transcriptomic abundance) of hydrocarbon monooxygense genes (HMOs) in the deep Gulf California, and the Guaymas basin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diversity of pHMOs in hydrocarbon plumes is much greater than previously appreciated.
we have identified a number of novel pHMO genes in the metagenome of the Guaymas plume and that these are transcriptionally active.
the diversity of pHMO genes in the environment is far greater than currently appreciated, and the majority of this diversity is not detectable with currently used PCR primers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diversity of pHMO genes and transcripts in the Guaymus Basin hydrothermal plume is greater than previously recognized.

the metatranscriptional analysis of the Guaymas hydrothermal plume revealed the presence of novel hydrocarbon monooxygeneases in the metagenomes and the metatranscripts of this natural deep sea hydrocarbon plume and the nearby background waters.
the diversity and abundance of pHMOs in the environment is much larger than currently appreciated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a large diversity of pHMO genes in the environment that have not been previously detected using conventional PCR primers and that these genes are active in situ in the environment.

the metatranscriptional approach is a powerful tool for the identification of novel genes and pathways in the environment, and that the use of metatranscriptomic data to infer gene function is a promising strategy to overcome the limitations of current PCR-based approaches.
we have identified a number of pHMOs that have not been detected before in marine environments, and we show that these genes are transcribed in the deep sea.
